To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Pathogen effectors from different kingdoms converge onto highly interconnected cellular hubs to subvert the Arabidopsis immune response; 2) The plant interactome is highly interconnected and is dominated by hubs; 3) Plant immune system proteins are highly connected and interact with effectors and hubs; 4) The majority of effectors and hubs are essential; and 5) Effectors interact directly with hubs, but not with plant immune receptors.
pathogens from different kingdoms converge on a limited set of plant immune system hubs to modulate defense.

understanding the molecular basis of plant immunity.
how plant cells recognize pathogen-derived molecules to mount effective defenses against microbial infection.
the molecular mechanisms of plant-pathogen interaction, and how these interactions have shaped plant immune system evolution.

“Pathogens deploy virulence proteins to interact with a limited number of highly connected cellular proteins to facilitate their diverse infection strategies.”

the host immune system is a complex network of proteins that can be targeted by pathogen effectors.
pathogens have evolved a diverse set of virulence effectors that converge upon a limited set of plant proteins to modulate the plant immune system.

plant immune system hubs, such as the TIR-NB-LRR proteins, interact with a wide range of proteins, and that pathogens from different lineages have independently evolved effectors that target these hubs to modulate plant immunity.
